# Practice a Job Interview With Le Chat: 5 Sample Questions and Instant Feedback

> **In short:** In about 15 minutes, you can run a full mock interview in Mistral's Le Chat (chat.mistral.ai) using 5 common questions, receive a sample strong answer for each, then improve your favorite answer with one follow-up prompt. A free account is enough; paid plans may answer faster during busy hours.

Whether you're prepping for your first real interview or just nervous about a callback, rehearsing out loud is the fastest way to find the rough edges in your answers. Le Chat is a friendly chat assistant built by Mistral, a French AI company, and it works just like sending messages to a friend. You ask a question, it answers — and you can ask it to play the interviewer, give you feedback, or even write a stronger version of what you said.

## Before you start

- **An account.** You can sign up at chat.mistral.ai with an email address or a Google account. The free tier is fine for this exercise.
- **A device with a browser.** Phone, tablet, or computer — any of them work. The screen will look slightly different on each.
- **Roughly 15 minutes.** Five questions, a couple of minutes thinking and writing each, plus one follow-up polish at the end.
- **A real job posting (optional but helpful).** If you have one open in another tab, Le Chat can tailor answers to the specific role. Without it, the answers will be more general — still useful, just less targeted.

One honest note before we start: Le Chat can draft and critique answers, but it cannot predict what your real interviewer will say. Treat the output as practice material, not as a script to memorize.

## Step 1 — Open Le Chat and start a fresh conversation

Open your browser and go to **chat.mistral.ai**. If you're not signed in, the button to look for reads **Log in** or **Sign up** in the top-right corner. After signing in, you land on a clean page with an empty chat box at the bottom labeled something like **Message Le Chat…**. Above the box you'll see a list of past chats on the left, or a **New chat** button if you've used it before.

Tap **New chat** (or just click into the empty box). The screen should turn into a blank conversation ready for your first message. If you see a welcome screen with example prompts, look for an **X**, **Skip**, or **Start chatting** button to dismiss it.

💬 Example: type nothing yet — just confirm you're on a fresh, blank chat.

You'll know it worked when the chat shows no old messages and the text box is empty.

## Step 2 — Set up Le Chat as your mock interviewer

Click into the message box and tell Le Chat what role you want it to play. This is called a **prompt** — just the instruction you give to the AI. A clear setup makes the rest of the session go smoothly. After you press **Enter** (or the **send** arrow), Le Chat usually replies within a few seconds with a short confirmation.

💬 Example:

> You are a friendly interviewer at a mid-sized company. Ask me one common interview question at a time, wait for my answer, then give me short feedback on what was strong and what I could tighten up. After 5 questions, wrap up with three overall tips. Start with question 1.

You'll know it worked when Le Chat replies with something like *"Great, let's get started. Question 1: …"*

If it dives straight into question 1 without acknowledging the setup, that's fine too — the role-play has begun either way.

## Step 3 — Answer question 1 out loud or in writing

Read the first question slowly. Give yourself a real moment to think, then write a draft answer — a few sentences is plenty. Don't try to make it perfect on the first try; the whole point is to have something Le Chat can react to. Press **Enter** to send.

💬 Example: if the question is *"Tell me about yourself,"* a starter answer could be:

> I'm a retail supervisor with four years of experience leading a team of eight. Before that I studied business in college. I enjoy solving problems for customers on the spot, and I'm now looking for a role where I can use those skills in an office setting.

You'll know it worked when Le Chat's reply names specific things you did well and suggests one or two small improvements.

## Step 4 — Go through all five questions the same way

Keep replying with your draft answers, one after another. Le Chat will move you to question 2, then 3, and so on, each time giving short feedback before the next question. You don't need to fix anything yet — just keep the rhythm of answer → feedback → next question. If a question catches you off guard (for example, *"What's your greatest weakness?"*), it's perfectly fine to type *"I'll be honest, I don't have a good answer ready, here's my best attempt…"* and then try.

💬 Example: when you reach the wrap-up, Le Chat's message will look something like:

> That's all five questions. Here are three overall tips: 1) lead with a concrete example more often, 2) keep answers around 60 seconds when spoken, 3) prepare one story you can adapt to many questions.

You'll know it worked when the wrap-up message arrives and you can see all five of your answers plus the feedback above them in the conversation thread.

## Step 5 — Pick one answer and ask Le Chat to strengthen it

Scroll back up to the question whose feedback most surprised you — usually the one with the most room to improve. Copy your own answer (or just click into the chat box again) and ask for a stronger version. Be specific about what you want: a short spoken version, a version that leads with a story, or a version that sounds less formal. Le Chat will rewrite it for you.

💬 Example:

> Can you rewrite my answer to question 2 ("What's your greatest weakness?") as a 60-second spoken answer that names a real weakness, shows what I'm doing about it, and ends on what I'm good at?

You'll know it worked when Le Chat returns a polished version you can picture yourself saying out loud.

## Step 6 — Save the polished answer and the tips

In the top-right corner of the chat, look for a button like **Share** or a copy icon — Le Chat can give you a link to the whole conversation. If that isn't there, simply select all the text in the conversation (`Ctrl+A` on a computer, long-press on mobile), copy it, and paste it into a note on your phone or a document. Saving the polished answer plus the three final tips means you have real rehearsal material the next time you practice.

💬 Example:

> Here are the five questions, my drafts, Le Chat's feedback, and the polished answer to question 2 — keep all of this together so you can re-read it before the real interview.

You'll know it worked when you can open that note tomorrow and see your polished answer without having to scroll through the chat again.

## Common mistakes

- **Sending a vague setup prompt.** If you just type *"Help me practice,"* Le Chat may not know to play the interviewer role. Always tell it the role, the number of questions, and what to do at the end.
- **Trying to make answer #1 perfect.** Your first draft is the practice material, not the final answer. The polishing happens in Step 5, so don't stall early.
- **Asking Le Chat to predict the real interview.** It can help you rehearse, but it doesn't know who you'll be meeting. Avoid prompts like *"What will they ask me?"* and stick to general common questions.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Mock interviews in Le Chat are a low-stress way to rehearse any kind of answer — a school presentation, a salary talk, even a tough message to a friend. Once you learn the "act as X, then give feedback" pattern, you can reuse it for almost anything.
- **For your business or work:** If you hire or mentor others, you can flip the same prompt and ask Le Chat to play the *candidate*. It's a quick way to see which questions reveal the most about a person.
- **If you're just getting started:** Run the session once without any prep at all. The point isn't a perfect answer today — it's noticing that the process is shorter and less scary than you imagined.

## Try it now

Open chat.mistral.ai in a new tab and send this single message:

> Pretend you are an interviewer. Ask me one common interview question and wait for my answer.

Type your honest first attempt — even two sentences is enough — and read the feedback. The whole thing takes under two minutes, and you'll already have one rehearsed answer before the day is out.
